properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 4 at 6:52AM CDT until October 4 at 9:45AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
FFWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Okaloosa County in northwestern Florida...

* Until 945 AM CDT.

* At 652 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Wright, Fort Walton Beach, Niceville, Destin, Eglin AFB,
Valparaiso, Mary Esther, Lake Lorraine, Ocean City, Shalimar, Cinco
Bayou, Eglin Village, Longwood, Postil and Seminole.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 4 at 6:33AM CDT until October 4 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southern Okaloosa County in northwestern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 633 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wright, Fort Walton Beach, Niceville, Destin, Eglin AFB,
Valparaiso, Mary Esther, Lake Lorraine, Ocean City, Shalimar,
Cinco Bayou, Longwood, Eglin Village, Postil, Seminole and
Wynnehaven Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County, Coastal Broward County and
Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 4 at 2:32AM EDT until October 5 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Alabama, including the following
areas, Geneva and Houston, Florida, including the following areas,
Calhoun, Coastal Franklin, Coastal Jefferson, Coastal Wakulla,
Gadsden, Inland Franklin, Inland Jefferson, Inland Wakulla,
Jackson, Leon, Madison, Northern Liberty and Southern Liberty, and

Brooks, Calhoun, Colquitt, Cook, Decatur, Dougherty, Early, Grady,
Irwin, Lanier, Lee, Lowndes, Miller, Mitchell, Randolph, Seminole,
Terrell, Thomas, Tift, Turner and Worth.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall totals of 2 to 6 inches are forecast for most
of the area with locally higher amounts of up to 10 inches
possible, especially along the Emerald Coast. Another area of
concern is across south-central Georgia where locally heavy rain
the past two afternoons has primed the region more so than the
rest of our area, so it wont take as much rain to cause flash
flooding. Additionally, very high rain rates due to the tropical
air mass in place may lead to flash flooding, especially in urban
and poor drainage areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 8:34PM CDT until October 8 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Shoal River Near Crestview affecting Okaloosa County.

For the Shoal River...including Crestview...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Shoal River near Crestview.

* WHEN...From Monday evening to Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Flooding becomes a threat to the Trevor
Court and Rattlesnake Bluff areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 4.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 11.0 feet
Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.1
feet on 09/12/1944.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates occur.
